xer.not_loaded: Not loaded yet: click Load and check.

xer.failed: The files could not be loaded: {err}
logs.note: Logs rotate (5 files of 1 MB each) and stay on this PC. The data folder also holds backups, the edit log and the XER store; the settings folder holds config.json.
upd.waiting: P6 MCP {latest} is ready. It installs as soon as these programs stop using P6 MCP: {names}.
upd.installing: Installing P6 MCP {latest}. P6 MCP restarts by itself in a moment.
upd.manual: This copy (portable or development) cannot update itself: use the download page.
upd.in_use:
P6 MCP is in use by: {names}.

Close P6 MCP in these programs now and update? They lose P6 MCP until you restart them (a write in progress is cancelled). Or the update installs by itself as soon as they close.
upd.note: Updates and the skill shop are the only network requests P6 MCP makes, both to GitHub. Updates: it asks GitHub for the latest release, then downloads the installer, checks its SHA256 against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt and installs it silently. Your MCP client settings are kept. Turn the option off to only check when you click Check now.
about.tagline: A local MCP server for Primavera P6 Professional databases and XER files.
about.privacy.text: P6 MCP runs only on this PC and sends nothing anywhere: it only reads GitHub for the optional update check and the skill shop (when you open it or ask for it; sharing a skill is done by you on GitHub). But the data its tools return goes to the AI model your MCP client uses, which may be a cloud service. For confidential schedules, use a local model.

ins.intro: Instructions are sent to the AI by every MCP client when it connects to P6 MCP. They apply to every conversation that uses the P6 tools.
ins.locked.tip: This rule protects the database: writes always need a dry run and your explicit yes.
ins.text: Instruction (one rule, written for the AI):
ins.custom.note: Example: When you show an activity, always write its Activity ID and name as Activity ID - Activity name (A1230 - Excavation), never the ID alone. Untick an instruction to keep it without sending it.
ins.restart: Click Save, then restart your MCP client (Claude Desktop, VS Code...) so that it reads the new instructions.
skill.intro: P6 skills are ready-made workflows that chain P6 tools (for example p6-weekly-update-review). Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Cline read them from their skills folder and use one when your request matches its description (install them on the MCP clients page); clients that support MCP prompts, such as Claude Desktop, also list them as prompts.
skill.col.title: Title
skill.share.note: Share sends one of your skills to the P6 MCP skill shop: the skill is copied to the clipboard and a GitHub form opens in your browser (a free GitHub account is needed): paste the skill and click Create. It is published once the maintainer approves it. Without an account, Export a zip file and send it: Import adds it here. The same zip can be uploaded as a skill in Claude Desktop.
skill.share.ask: Share the skill {name} publicly in the P6 MCP skill shop ({repo})? P6 MCP copies the skill to the clipboard and opens the GitHub form in your browser: sign in if asked (or create a free GitHub account), paste the skill in the Skill field (Ctrl+V), tick the license box and click Create. It is published under the Apache-2.0 license after the maintainer's review. Never share client names or project data.
skill.share.invalid: This skill cannot be shared yet: {err}
skill.share.copied: The skill is on the clipboard: paste it in the Skill field of the GitHub form (Ctrl+V), then click Create.
skill.restart: Click Save, then click Update skills on the MCP clients page (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Cline) and restart your MCP client for the prompts.

skill.f.text.note: Write {argument} where an input value goes, for example {project}. Name the P6 tools to use (p6_project_summary...): a skill naming a tool the current settings do not offer is not offered. The description says what the skill does and when to use it: clients pick a skill by it. The P6 rules (IDs, last F9, two-step writes) are added at the end automatically.
skill.f.files.note: Text files written beside SKILL.md (checklists, thresholds, examples): at most {n}, {size} characters each, .md, .txt, .csv or .json. Mention them in the instructions so the AI reads them. Scripts are not allowed.

Read a skill before installing it: a skill is instructions for the AI, and one that uses write tools can change your schedule after your confirmation.
